title: Microsoft Edge: vertical tabs update
summary: Hold: the briefing assures readers that browser-wide Edge policies are unaffected by the rebuild, but no Microsoft source checked supports that assurance. The roadmap details and the Group Policy and registry references are supported.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Existing vertical tabs is a user-operated alternative layout with tabs down the side instead of at the top.
claims.quote: Configures whether a user can access an alternative layout where tabs are vertically aligned on the side of the browser instead of at the top.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: impact
claims.claim: With VerticalTabsAllowed enabled or not configured, tabs remain at the top and the user can turn on vertical tabs.
claims.quote: If you enable or don't configure this policy, the tab layout remains at the top, but a user has the option to turn on vertical tabs on the side.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling VerticalTabsAllowed removes vertical tabs as an option for users.
claims.quote: If you disable this policy, then the vertical tab layout isn't available as an option for users.

claims.claim: The Group Policy control is Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Configures availability of a vertical layout for tabs on the side of the browser.
claims.quote:
GP name: Configures availability of a vertical layout for tabs on the side of the browser
GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge

claims.claim: The policy has registry path SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge, value VerticalTabsAllowed, type REG_DWORD.
claims.quote:
Registry settings
Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge
Value name: VerticalTabsAllowed
Value type: REG\_DWORD
